findings.claim: A task/node with multiple outstanding interrupts can be prematurely re-executed after only a partial resume unless the runtime tracks enough per-task interrupt/resume state to keep it suspended.
primary_evidence: langchain-ai/langgraph issue #6208 is maintainer/collaborator-authored and describes the pre-fix limitation: a node with two interrupts could rerun after one resume because stored metadata did not track enough pending resume/interrupt information
langchain-ai/langgraph PR #6158 merged 2025-10-06, merge commit 6cc889981854b12acb1dad406adf5d517e8a22f2, implements selective interrupt task scheduling for sync and async loops

PR #6158 changed _loop.py to aggregate interrupt writes, count resumes per task, derive skipped_task_ids, and raise GraphInterrupt while incomplete resumes remain; main.py excludes skipped_task_ids from execution

PR #6158 adds sync and async tests named test_node_with_multiple_interrupts_requires_full_resume plus sequential-resume tests; the test contract states the node must not re-execute until valid resume values have been supplied for all interrupts
findings.scope_correction: Issue #6208 is still open and its body describes the earlier limitation even though the later merged PR body says it solves #6208 and the merged patch contains the multi-interrupt implementation/tests. Treat the merged commit/tests as evidence that this specific implementation was added, not as proof that every current LangGraph release/runtime deployment retains identical semantics without a pinned release/current-code reproduction.

findings.claim: AutoGen GraphFlow can be reported as complete after interruption/resume while saved coordination state still has remaining work but no ready/enqueued successor.
primary_evidence: microsoft/autogen issue #7043 is open, labeled needs-triage, and supplies a resume scenario where the workflow emits 'Digraph execution is complete' while the saved GraphManager state has remaining work, enqueued_any=false, and ready=[]
the issue reports Python 3.11 and Python dev/main branch rather than a pinned release/commit; it remains unassigned and open
findings.scope_correction: This is a reporter-supplied reproduction/state snapshot, not a maintainer-confirmed root cause or merged-fix regression. It directly supports the invariant shape 'remaining work + empty ready/enqueued state is incompatible with authoritative completion' only within the reported GraphFlow scenario. It does not establish prevalence, current-release persistence, or the reporter's proposed atomic-transition root cause.

phase1_implication: Partial-resume scheduling requires generation/task-local obligation accounting, and completion must not be inferred solely from an empty ready queue when durable remaining-work state contradicts it. These are mechanism-specific safety precedents, not a generic parity proof.
exact_next_verification: Fresh bootstrap. Probe evaluation/LATEST once for the root20/config6 checker-v2 durable precommit and three controls. If absent, rotate to FE-383 (OpenAI Agents Python HITL resume unsent tool-output provenance) and independently verify issue #3004, merged PR #3006, and changed tests; prioritize whether the dedup bug is specifically server-managed conversation hydration and whether the fix distinguishes generated-local from server-acknowledged outputs.
